''Cycas jenkinsiana'' Griff. | synonyms_ref = }} '''''Cycas pectinata''''' is a species of ''[[Cycas]]'', the fourth to be named; it was described in 1826 by Scottish surgeon and botanist [[Francis Buchanan-Hamilton]] from [[Kamrup region|Kamrup]], Assam in [[northeast India]]. The species is one of the most widespread cycads. It is found in the northeastern part of [[India]] ([[Assam]], [[Manipur]], [[Meghalaya]], [[Sikkim]], [[Darjeeling]]), [[Nepal]], [[Bhutan]], [[Burma|Myanmar]], southern [[China]] ([[Yunnan]]), [[Bangladesh]], [[Malaysia]], [[Cambodia]], northern [[Thailand]], [[Laos]], and [[Vietnam]].Hill, K.D. 1998-2012. http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/cycadpg?taxname=Cycas%20pectinataRita Singh & Khuraijam Jibankumar Singh, 2010. {{cite web |url=http://ehsst.org/Pleione%20Contents%204.2.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-06-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714125715/http://ehsst.org/Pleione%20Contents%204.2.pdf |archive-date=2014-07-14 }}Pant, D.D., Singh, R. & Chauhan, D.K. 1994. Telopea 11(4):463 – 488 In China, it grows in dry, open thickets in limestone mountains and red soil in sparse [[monsoon]] forests.Fu Shu-hsia, Cheng Wan-chün, Fu Li-kuo & Chen Chia-jui. 1978. Popularis Sin. 7: 4-17 http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=3&taxon_id=200005229 ''Cycas pectinata'' grows up to {{convert|40|ft|m}} tall and has very large, ovoid male cones. The tallest ''Cycas pectinata'' is a female plant in North [[Kamrup district|Kamrup]], Assam which measures {{convert|52.8|ft|m}}. The tree is the world's tallest ''Cycas'' plant.Khuraijam Jibankumar Singh & Rita Singh, 2012. http://www.indianforester.co.in/index.php/indianforester/article/view/29048 In Northeast India, the species is under severe threat due to clearing of forest and overcollection of male cones for preparation of traditional medicines.Khuraijam Jibankumar Singh & Rita Singh, 2014. Population assessment and distribution of ''Cycas pectinata'' Buchanan-Hamilton in Northeast India, Pleione 8(1): 17 - 25.Khuraijam Jibankumar Singh & Rita Singh. 2012. The ethnobotany of ''Cycas'' in the states of Assam and Meghalaya, India. Proceedings of 8th International Conference on Cycad Biology, Panama. Memoirs of The New York Botanical Garden. The New York Botanical Garden: New York. http://www.cycadsofindia.in/p/recent-publications.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211081455/http://www.cycadsofindia.in/p/recent-publications.html |date=2017-02-11 }} The species is listed in [[CITES Appendix II]] and [[IUCN Red List]]. ==Historical information== ''Cycas pectinata'' was described by Hamilton in 1826 from "''On the hills which bound Bengal to the east''" with its habitat at "''Camrupae sylvis''".Hamilton. 1826. Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 5(2): 322-323, figs 3, 5 [[Undivided Kamrup district|Kamrup]] (''Camrupae'') is a district in [[Assam]] (Northeast India). ==Morphology== Tall evergreen trees with crown of leaves at the apex of trunk. Stems robust, glabrous at base and usually branched when mature. Leaves 1 to 2 m long, dark green. Male cones usually large, cylindrically ovoid and yellowish or orange in maturity. [[Megasporophyll|Megasporophylls]] deeply pectinate and densely covered with hairs. Seeds ovoid, [[Glabrous leaves|glabrous]] and orange to red-yellow on maturity.{{Cite web |title=Cycas pectinata in Flora of China @ efloras.org |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200005229 |access-date=2026-05-27 |website=www.efloras.org}} ==Uses== ===Economic=== ''Cycas pectinata'' is a popular ornamental plant grown in gardens and at public places.{{Cite web |title=Cycas pectinata |url=http://www.llifle.net/Encyclopedia/PALMS_AND_CYCADS/Family/Cycadaceae/28863/Cycas_pectinata |access-date=2025-08-16 |website=www.llifle.net}} In Assam, green mature leaves are used to decorate large numbers of temporary shrines called "Pooja Pandals," erected to worship deities during festivals. The leaves are used for decoration of the entrance of the marriage pandals and bouquets.{{Cite web |title=Cycas pectinata |url=http://www.llifle.net/Encyclopedia/PALMS_AND_CYCADS/Family/Cycadaceae/28863/Cycas_pectinata |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=www.llifle.net}}. ===Traditional=== Young fronds are eaten as vegetables in [[Manipur]] and [[Sikkim]].{{Cite journal |last=Haokip |first=L. Lhingkhotin |last2=Panmei |first2=Robert |date=2022-08-07 |title=Lesser-known wild edible plants used by Thadou-Kuki tribe of Indo-Myanmar region, Manipur, India |url=https://smujo.id/biodiv/article/view/11116 |journal=Biodiversitas Journal of Biological Diversity |language=en |volume=23 |issue=8 |doi=10.13057/biodiv/d230817 |issn=2085-4722|doi-access=free }} Seeds of ''Cycas pectinata'' are traditionally utilized as a source of starch by indigenous tribes and are eaten raw or roasted in Assam and the bordering region of [[Meghalaya]]. Microsporophylls are chewed raw to cure stomach-aches and ulcers. The young microsporophylls are eaten by young men in Meghalaya and Assam to enhance male sexual potency.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}} ===Vietnam=== In Vietnam, cycas pectinata are called Hundred Year tree (Cây thiên tuế) and are considered as auspicious ornamental plants. Large cycads are often placed in front of mansions and corporate or government offices. {{Cite web |last=admin |date=2019-01-21 |title=Ý nghĩa phong thủy và tác dụng của cây thiên tuế, vạn tuế {{!}} PGR Việt Nam - Kiến thức thực vật và dược liệu |url=https://pgrvietnam.org.vn/y-nghia-phong-thuy-va-tac-dung-cua-cay-thien-tue-van-tue-5282.html |access-date=2026-08-27 |language=en-US}} ==Conservation efforts== [[Image:Cycas_pectinata_conservation.jpg|thumb|A group of participants of the program ''Yendang: the Living Fossil'' holding a poster]] In [[Northeast India]], two conservation programs are in place for the conservation of ''Cycas pectinata'' populations in the state of [[Assam]] and [[Manipur]].Khuraijam Jibankumar Singh & Rita Singh. 2012. Cycad conservation and its challenges in India. In Bhattacharya and Garg (eds) News challenges: New opportunities in environment. McMillan: New Delhi In 2014, '''''Yendang'': The Living Fossil''', a cycad conservation program involving indigenous tribes and state forest department started in one of the cycad localities of Manipur (''Yendang'' is the local name of ''Cycas pectinata'' in Manipur). From 2015 onwards, cycadologists and cycad lovers have organised the Cycad Volleyball Tournament in Manipur to create awareness among the locals and to lead youth to take part in protecting the cycad populations. {{Clear}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Wikispecies}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q5197929}} [[Category:Cycas|Pectinata]] [[Category:Flora of the Indian subcontinent]] [[Category:Flora of Indo-China]] [[Category:Flora of Yunnan]] [[Category:Plants described in 1826]] [[Category:Trees of temperate climates]]
